headline: Europe Reconnects 3,740 km of Rivers by Removing 603 Barriers
meta_description: Europe removed a record 603 obsolete river barriers in 2025, reconnecting thousands of kilometers of waterways across 21 countries and restoring fish migration.
summary_short: In a landmark year for river restoration, Europe tore down 603 obsolete barriers in 2025, reconnecting 3,740 km of rivers and enabling fish migration for the fifth conse…
body:
Europe tore down a record 603 obsolete river barriers in 2025, reconnecting 3,740 kilometers of waterways across 21 countries and restoring passage for migrating fish.

This achievement marks the fifth consecutive year of progress in large-scale river restoration, signaling a sustained commitment to undoing decades of fragmentation. The removal of these barriers—dams, weirs, and other structures that once divided rivers into isolated segments—allows fish populations to move freely again, restoring natural breeding and feeding patterns that had been disrupted for generations.

The scale of the effort demonstrates what coordinated action across borders can accomplish. With 21 countries participating, the initiative shows that river restoration has moved from isolated local projects to a continent-wide priority, driven by both environmental necessity and recognition that connected rivers support healthier ecosystems, stronger fish stocks, and more resilient freshwater systems.
quick_facts: 3,740 kilometers of waterways reconnected across Europe
21 countries participated in the removal effort
Fifth consecutive year of annual progress on restoration
